# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment.

Plain HTML static site root with index.html. Great. We can build a single-page game with HTML/CSS/JS, no build step. Use canvas or DOM? For fake-ad minigames, DOM+CSS is great, tactile.

Let's design "AdPlay" — a collection of 6 playable ad-style minigames, each with a fake ad wrapper (skip countdown, fake app store chrome) and a "real game" under it. The humor: ads that don't match gameplay. We should make levels genuinely fun and playable, mobile responsive, touch and mouse.

Concept: A vertical phone frame with fake ad UI: top "AD" badge, progress dots, sound toggle, bottom fake CTA button ("Install Now", "Play Now"). Each level starts with 5-second skip timer; if you skip, you miss... Actually core loop should be playing. Design as: "AdPlay: 100% Real Gameplay (Definitely)" — six ad genres. Each ad is a tiny level; complete objective to earn stars/tips. After each level show ironic "ad" interstitial? Keep it tight.

Better: The app is a game where you're a "playtester" hired by sketchy mobile game studios. Each level is one of those ads, with a trick: the ads lie, and you must play the real version. But simpler: just deliver good minigames.

Minigames ideas (simple physics/canvas/DOM):
1. "Rescue the Dog" (pull pin / save from bees) — drag a wooden plank to deflect a falling beehive / block lava? This is complex. Maybe simplified: "Save the Doge" — draw a line to shield dog from bee swarm. Player draws a barrier with mouse/touch across a play field, physics-ish bees fall. Implement with canvas particles and line segments? Could be fun.

2. "Hero Rescue" — pull pins in order to let lava flow to monster and treasure to hero without killing hero. Puzzle with pins. Complex but doable with canvas and simple physics/slots? Could be grid-based pin puzzle: tap pins to release colored liquid, route to targets. Hmm.

3. "Number Merge Tower" — tap numbered gates to multiply your squad and storm the castle. Classic "count masters" crowd runner. Could implement a lane runner where you pick left/right gates with +5 x2 and avoid spikes, ending in boss. That's very ad-like. Do 3 lanes? Use simple auto-runner with 2 choices at gates, tap left/right. Very fun and simple.

4. "Pull the Pin" — lift pin to drop balls into cup, avoid bombs. Could do simple 2D physics.

5. "Tile Match / Sort" — "only 1% can solve" — match 3 or sort screw puzzle. A quick "connect pipes" or "water sort". Water sort is easy to implement and compelling: tubes of colored water, pour to sort. Very ad-like.

6. "Idle / money" — tap to build. Less action.

7. "Bridge builder" — draw a bridge within budget, car drives across physics. Hard but impressive.

8. "Knife hit / spin" — tap to throw knives into rotating log, avoid hitting knives. Very ad-like, easy to implement, satisfying. Include "wood log rotates, tap to throw knife".

9. "Helix jump" — ball bounces down rotating helix, avoid red. Could implement 2D-ish. Maybe not.

10. "Traffic jam / parking" — too hard.

11. "Cut the rope" style — maybe.

12. "Monster eat city / snake" — classic "snake vs numbers": move snake, eat smaller numbers, grow, avoid bigger. This is excellent ad material ("Snake.io"). Implement top-down arena with joystick / pointer movement and number enemies. Fun.

We need a complete game with progression, stars, level select, score, sound, persistence. 5 levels is a good scope. Let's pick 5 genres with distinct mechanics:

Level 1: "Squad Rush" — count masters gate runner (left/right choices, multiply/add, obstacles, final boss). Action.
Level 2: "Knife Spin" — timing tap, 20 knives into a rotating log, don't hit existing. Skill.
Level 3: "Snake Bites" — arena snake.io vs numbered blobs, eat smaller, avoid bigger. Action/strategy.
Level 4: "Color Sort" — water sort puzzle with 6 tubes. Puzzle.
Level 5: "Dog Rescue" — draw a shield line to protect dog from falling bees. Creative.
Maybe Level 6: "Pull the Pin" ball drop? Could be bonus. 5 levels enough if polished.

Alternatively, each level presented as a fake ad with timer then "Skip" after 5s; playing and winning before skip gets "3-star" and a "tip". But timers may frustrate. We can implement the ad framing: "AD • 0:05" skip button, and a fake "X" close button; if you close, you exit to level select. Winning shows "You beat the ad!" with stars based on performance. Cute.

Better framing: The whole game is "AdPlay" — ad-free? The humor: you're playing an ad, and every level has a fake ad overlay. We'll implement:
- Landing screen: logo, tagline "Every level is the ad. None of it is the game." with Play button, level carousel grid, total stars, "Ad blocker: OFF" toggle for humor.
- Each level has top ad bar: "AD" badge, sponsor name ("Royal Flush Games"), mute, and skip countdown. Skip appears after 3 seconds. Clicking skip goes back to menu with confirmation? No confirmation; simply exits (as ads do), with a fun toast "You skipped the ad. The ad remembers." But accidentally skipping is bad. Place skip at corner; also play area not blocked.
- Level intro card (fake app store page) with icon, title, rating 4.9, "Install" CTA that starts level. Actually users want to play, so start after tapping Play. Could make intro quick: full-screen "ad" card saying "MEGA SALE 99% OFF" then gameplay reveals? Might slow replay. Keep intro minimal: level card with objective and big "PLAY THE AD" button. Each level's instructions one sentence.

- Win: overlay with stars (3 criteria per level), score, "NEXT AD" / "REPLAY" / "LEVELS". Losing: "The ad got you" retry.

- Persistence: localStorage stars/best.

- Sound: WebAudio synth (no assets). Toggle.

- Responsive: Full viewport app with landscape support? Mobile-first portrait but levels fit. Use 9:16 stage max 520x860, but desktop can show frame with decorative background. Support keyboard (arrow/space) and touch.

- Accessibility: buttons, aria-live announcements, reduced motion.

Implementation architecture: plain JS modules? Static server supports JS. Use separate files: index.html, styles.css, js/main.js, js/audio.js, js/engine.js maybe. Keep manageable. A single app.js could be 2000+ lines. We can split levels into files as ES modules: levels/squad.js etc. Need to ensure no module CORS issues (server fine, file:// not but deployment serves). Could use modules.

Let's plan code carefully.

Core:
- index.html with app shell:
  - #app
  - header with logo, stars
  - #screen-home, #screen-game
  - game screen: fake ad chrome: topbar with AD badge / level name / skip; #stage; footer with CTA tip banner maybe.
  - overlays: #modal level intro? Use modal for win/lose and level briefing.
  - toast.
- CSS: modern, saturated "hyper-casual ad" aesthetic: gradient backgrounds, chunky rounded shapes, bold font (system font stack with maybe Google font? Offline environment; avoid external fonts for reliability; use 'Arial Black', system). Could embed an SVG logo. Use CSS-only confetti.

- Main JS: router, state, level registry.
  - State: stars per level, sound, skip logic.
  - Game loop management: each level module exposes {id,title,studio,tagline,objective,theme, start(container, api), destroy()}. API: win(score, stats), lose(reason), setHint, sound.
  - Level lifecycle: when starting, destroy previous, show stage, create canvas etc. Ad skip starts at 3s; skip button exits to home. Win overlay after delay.

Need levels robust.

Level 1: SQUAD RUSH (crowd gate runner).
Mechanics:
- Canvas 2D, portrait stage ~ width 420 height 620 (logical). Player squad represented by a blob of dots (count). Auto-run upward (screen scroll down). At intervals, a gate row with two choices: e.g., "+15" and "x2" or "-10" / "÷2"? Need choose best, displayed in big numbers. On passing gate, count updates. Obstacles (spikes) kill some. At end boss with HP = count? Goal: reach boss with enough squad (>= 40) to defeat. Win condition: reach castle; if count >= bossHP win else lose. But if gates are obvious, no fail. Add target: Boss HP 60, squad shrinks at spikes, gates random. Add timing: player can swipe/tap left/right to steer? In classic, squad auto-shifts to gate half. export function createStage(container) {
  container.innerHTML = '<canvas class="game-canvas"></canvas>';
  const canvas = ...
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  let w=0,h=0,dpr=1;
  function resize() {
    const rect = container.getBoundingClientRect();
    w = Math.max(320, rect.width); h = Math.max(420, rect.height);
    dpr = Math.min(2, window.devicePixelRatio||1);
    canvas.width = Math.floor(w*dpr); canvas.height = Math.floor(h*dpr);
    canvas.style.width = w+'px'; ...
    ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0);
  }
  const ro = new ResizeObserver(resize); ro.observe(container); resize();
  return {canvas, ctx, get w(){...}, ...}
}
```
Since functions need current w/h, expose object with getters and `onResize` callback list.

export function createLoop(update, draw) {
 let raf; let last=0; let running=true;
 function frame(t){ if(!running) return; const dt=Math.min(0.05,(t-last)/1000||0.016); last=t; update(dt); draw(); raf=requestAnimationFrame(frame);}
 raf=requestAnimationFrame(frame);
 return { stop(){running=false;cancelAnimationFrame(raf);}, };
}
```

```js
export function createStage(container) {
  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
  canvas.className='game-canvas';
  container.appendChild(canvas);
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  let w=0,h=0,dpr=1;
  const cbs=[];
  const ro = new ResizeObserver(()=>resize());
  ro.observe(container);
  function resize(){
    const r=container.getBoundingClientRect();
    w=Math.max(240,r.width); h=Math.max(320,r.height);
    dpr=Math.min(2,window.devicePixelRatio||1);
    canvas.width=Math.round(w*dpr); canvas.height=Math.round(h*dpr);
    canvas.style.width=w+'px'; canvas.style.height=h+'px';
    ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0);
    cbs.forEach(f=>f(w,h));
  }
  resize immediately but container might have layout; use rAF? getBoundingClientRect right after display should be ok.
  return {
    canvas, ctx,
    get w(){return w}, get h(){return h},
    onResize(fn){cbs.push(fn); return ()=>...}
    destroy(){ro.disconnect(); canvas.remove()}
  }
}
```

We can create an SVG sprite sheet? Could embed sprite images generated as SVG files, and load into canvas. But drawing with canvas is fine and can be considered sprites if we render pre-made offscreen canvases. To satisfy "sprites from a bunch of collected ads", we could create a sprite system: procedurally generated sprite sheets (PNG or SVG) for characters. We can create SVG sprite files per level and use them as images with Canvas drawImage. That enhances the "collected ads" feel. We can also add a "Sprite Vault" home element saying "Sprites borrowed from 5 suspicious ads" (original recreations). Hmm. Could draw these as canvas using drawImage from preloaded SVG images. However, vector-drawn-on-canvas at runtime is more flexible and still art. But to specifically answer "using sprites", let's add an asset sprite system. We have no real ad assets and shouldn't use copyrighted ones. We'll create an original `assets/sprites.svg` sprite sheet with symbols and a manifest, plus a SpriteSheet loader. Using `` with SVG fragments (`sprites.svg#id`) is tricky in canvas. Alternative: make individual SVG files per sprite, load with Image, drawImage. That's simple and robust. messages.text: Ranging from survivor.io levels to bullet hell levels, pretty much just base the game on ads that are quite common for the average mobile gamer

content.text:
The user clarifies further: levels ranging from survivor.io to bullet hell, based on common mobile game ads. So we should broaden level selection: survivor.io-style horde survival, bullet hell, plus common ad genres. Our current 5: crowd runner, knife, snake, water sort, dog rescue. Need include survivor.io-style (auto-shooter horde survival) and bullet hell. Maybe replace some or add more levels. Scope could be 7 levels:

1. Squad Rush (crowd runner) — common ad.
2. Bullet Heaven (bullet hell / dodge) — common ad "only 1% can dodge".
3. Survivor Isle (survivor.io-style auto-shooter horde).
4. Knife Spin (knife hit).
5. Snake Bites (snake.io).
6. Potion Sort (water sort).
7. Dog Rescue (save the dog).

That's 7 levels. More work but doable. Need quality. The user explicitly wants survivor.io levels and bullet hell levels. Let's add both as levels. Could drop Knife or Snake? No, more variety is good, but build complexity. 7 levels with 2 new mechanics = significant but manageable. We have plenty of token budget. Let's design:

Level "SURVIVOR ISLE" (survivor.io style):
- Top-down auto-shooter. Player character auto-fires at nearest enemy; player moves with pointer/WASD. Enemies spawn in waves around arena and chase. Survive 30s or kill 40 enemies? Ads show "survive the night" with horde. Implement 30-second survival with XP pickups and level-ups? Ads often show choosing upgrades. For a mini-game, add quick level-up choice cards (3 choices: +fire rate, +damage, +projectile) that pause briefly. That's very survivor.io and fun. But UI overlays and gameplay state. Could be done.
- Core: arena dark grass/island, player with gun auto-aims, bullets. Enemies (slimes/zombies) spawn at edges and chase; colliding damages player with brief invulnerability. Health 100. Survive 30s; kills spawn gems that magnetize when close; XP levels grant upgrade choice at 4 thresholds. Show progress bar. Win by surviving 30s; stars by health remaining. Score kills.
- Controls: pointer drag / WASD movement; player auto-shoots nearest enemy every 0.5s. This is easy to pick up.
- Sprites: player sprite, enemy sprites, bullet, gem, weapon icons. Need new assets: survivor hero, zombie/slime, gem, maybe bullet drawn. Could reuse runner sprite for hero? Better create hero sprite (top-down) and monster blob. Add assets: survivor.svg (character with gun viewed top-down/3/4), monster.svg (purple slime zombie), gem.svg (cyan crystal), xp? maybe.
- Upgrade modal: DOM overlay with 3 cards; level pauses. Each card icon/text. Choices apply. Use DOM overlay inside stage with buttons. Need pointer capture not interfering. Could draw canvas cards and handle clicks; DOM nicer and accessible. Implement `showUpgrade()` overlay div; pause update; on choose, resume. Level 6 maybe. Not too hard.

- Enemy spawn: every 0.55s, spawn 1-3 at random edge; HP scales over time. Bullets damage. On death, drop gem; gems attract when within 90px; collecting gives XP; XP thresholds 3,7,12,18; on level up show upgrades. Survival timer 30s; final 8s horde surge. Health regen? no. Hearts? health 100, enemy hit -12, iframe 1s. Enemies despawn? no cap 60. Bullet auto-fire at nearest within 380px, projectile speed 520, damage 26, fire interval 0.45; enemies HP 30 + t*? With upgrades, manageable.
- Win at 30s. Stars: 1 survive; 2 health>=50; 3 health>=80. Score kills.
- HUD: health bar, timer ring, level, XP bar, kill count. Canvas.
- Player body top-down: survivor sprite rotated? Draw sprite facing nearest enemy (sprite designed facing right, rotate). Maybe simpler sprite always upright but gun points aim; sprite body drawn with drawImage not rotated to avoid looking odd; rotate whole sprite to aim is typical top-down. Create survivor facing right. Fine.
- Enemies top-down small slime with eyes, bounce; use new `slime.svg`. 
- Background: island dark with grid/ grass patches, water border? Survivor.io jungle. Draw dark green arena with scattered grass, bones, glowing pickups.
- Add auto-fire muzzle flash and hit particles.

Level "BULLET HELL" (bullet dodge):
- Common mobile ad: tiny ship/character dodging incoming bullets, "only 1% can survive 20 seconds", often "bullet hell" ads with a heart. Implement a tight bullet-hell arena: control a small character with mouse/touch drag or keyboard; survive 20 seconds while bullets in patterns (spiral, aimed, walls). No shooting? Bullet hell ads often have auto-shooting or pure dodge. Could add auto-fire at a boss for spice: player is a small ship shooting a giant eye? "Bullet Heaven" maybe. Simpler: survive 20s; player has 1 hit point with tiny hitbox (bullet hell standard) or 3 hearts. Ads commonly "can you survive 30s". Add slow-motion focus? Let's do 3 hearts, 18s, patterns escalate.
- Player: small glowing heart/orb with trail, movement follow pointer directly (smoothed) or keyboard. Tiny hitbox radius 5. Bullets colorful orbs. Spawn patterns:
  - aimed shots from top/sides;
  - rotating spiral from center for 4s;
  - horizontal rain waves with gaps;
  - ring bursts.
- Set pieces scheduled by time. Total 20s. HUD shows timer and hearts, progress bar. 
- Stars: 1 survive, 2 survive with >=2 hearts, 3 no damage.
- Score = time survived + graze? Maybe count grazes (near miss) as score, ad-like "CLOSE CALLS". Stars based on hearts. Score = grazes; best.
- Visual: neon bullet-hell on dark vortex, player a small white/cyan heart; bullets pink/cyan with glow; screen shake on hit; particles. Use `heart` sprite? Player heart drawn vector or sprite. Create `ship.svg` maybe. Bullet hell ads often feature a tiny white square/heart. Let's create `fighter.svg` (small cyan ship/heart).
- Add slow-mo when holding? Not needed.
- Controls: pointer/touch drag; keyboard arrows. Mobile drag.
- Bullets from offscreen, patterns, can despawn; speed ~100-200. Hitbox with graze radius 20 for score.
- Need fairness: 3 hearts.
- Timer 20s. Stars.
- Level icon "💥" or "🌀".

Order levels maybe:
1. Squad Rush (crowd runner)
2. Survivor Isle (horde survival)
3. Bullet Heaven (bullet hell)
4. Knife Spin
5. Snake Bites
6. Potion Sort
7. Dog Rescue

Or put bullet hell earlier. Home supports 7 cards; scroll. Total stars /21. Need update copy to 7 playable ads. Header "SEASON 01 · 7 PLAYABLE ADS". Continue label. Fineprint. Maybe group categories. Level list 7 rows; home scrolls. On mobile 844, hero ~330 + 7 cards ~500 + footer = scroll; fine. Could make cards two-column grid to fit: 2 cols x 4 rows, compact 96px cards with icon+title+stars. That looks like an app store. Let's redesign level list as 2-column grid of cards with icon tile top-left, title, studio, stars. 7 cards; last spans? Use two columns; on narrow 320, still okay. Each card height ~110. 4 rows => 440 + hero 300 = 740 + header = 800; close. Could make cards 92px. We'll see.
- Or show a horizontal snap carousel of larger cards; 7 cards scroll horizontally. That's mobile-friendly and showcases art. But visibility of all levels less. The 2-col grid is better.

Need update copy: "SEVEN ridiculous ads", "7 PLAYABLE ADS", total stars 21. Also help. Fine.

Now, the user said "using sprites from a bunch of collected ads that viewers may experience on there mobile device." We created original sprites. Add a "SPRITE VAULT" note maybe not necessary. Help modal can mention "All sprites are original recreations — no actual ads were harmed." Good.

Need create new sprites:
- survivor.svg — top-down hero with gun facing right. Character circle head, body, arm + blaster pointing right.
- slime.svg — purple/green monster with eyes, claws. Top-down facing right.
- gem.svg — cyan XP crystal.
- fighter.svg — small cyan ship/orb with white heart core? Bullet hell player. Maybe a tiny angel/heart. Let's make a small "star fighter" with wings, cyan and white, pointing up (rotation 0 up). For direct movement, no rotation.
- bullet? draw circles with glow.
- maybe boss.svg for bullet hell: giant eye at top? Bullet hell ads often have a boss. Could add a hovering boss eye that fires patterns, making the scene more interesting. Create `eye-boss.svg`. Draw at top center behind patterns, bobbing; not interactive. Great.
- survivor enemy variants maybe one slime enough; tint for elites? Use draw sprite with alpha and scale; elites bigger with more HP.

Now implement.

We also should consider using sprites for all levels:
- Squad: runner sprites, coin, bomb, ogre, castle, bush/cloud.
- Knife: knife, apple, log drawn.
- Snake: snake-head, orbs, gem? use orbs.
- Sort: potion liquids drawn; maybe flower background.
- Rescue: dog, bee, cloud, bush, flower.
- Survivor: survivor, slime, gem.
- Bullet: fighter, eye-boss; bullets vector.
Great, sprite variety.

Need write sprite loader and all level files. This is a large task. Let's proceed methodically.

First finish CSS. Need classes for all screens and overlays. Let's write a comprehensive styles.css. Plan:

Global:
```
:root { colors, font; }
* { box-sizing:border-box; }
html,body { margin:0; height:100%; }
body { background:#12081f; color:#fff; font-family:...; overflow:hidden; overscroll-behavior:none; }
button { font:inherit; color:inherit; cursor:pointer; }
```

Ambient desktop: fixed full; gradient blobs; ambient words rotated vertical or horizontal at sides; hidden below 1100px.

#app: width min(100vw, 470px); height 100dvh; margin auto; position relative; overflow hidden; background #170b26; display flex; flex-direction column; box-shadow on desktop; border radius on desktop if height less? Use media min-width 640px: height:min(920px, calc(100dvh - 40px)); border-radius:36px; border. On mobile height:100dvh.
But capture desktop 1440x900: app 430x860 centered. Good.
Screens absolute inset 0; display flex column; hidden attribute display none. `screen[hidden]{display:none}`. Home overflow-y:auto.

Home:
- background gradient with pseudo dots. Padding.
- header flex, brand mark yellow rounded square with play triangle.
- hero padding; h1 clamp 40-52; font-weight 900; letter-spacing -0.03em; line-height .88; em italic? Use font-style normal with color yellow and maybe skew. `.period` coral.
- season pill.
- play button big pill with gradient yellow, black text, box-shadow 0 6px 0 #b98700; active translate.
- hero stats.
- level list grid 2 columns; card dark glass; active press; stars row; icon tile with gradient per level via inline style CSS variables (--c1,--c2). Number badge.
- footer ticker fixed at bottom of home; gradient mask; marquee animation. Home main padding-bottom to avoid.

Ticker CSS: `.ticker` height 34; overflow hidden; `.ticker-track{display:flex;gap:26px;white-space:nowrap;animation:ticker 28s linear infinite;}`.

Game:
- `.game` background #0d0616. adbar 36px flex; ad badge yellow bg black text; sponsor; skip button ghost with border; enabled pulse.
- game titlebar 56px; round buttons; title. 
- stage flex:1; position relative; overflow hidden; background black; touch-action none.
- `.game-canvas { display:block; width:100%; height:100%; }` set by helper.
- hint-chip absolute top 12 left 50%, transform; dark pill; opacity transition; `.show`.
- ad banner 46px with gradient pink; text; fake CTA black. On mobile safe area bottom padding.
- result-layer absolute inset 0; background rgba; display flex; align center; z-index 20; backdrop-filter blur. hidden handling.
- Result card: dark panel with border, rounded; stars large; buttons. Add variants. Confetti absolute.
- Modal help could use result layer style but on home; easier create help overlay element dynamically and append to app with shared `.sheet-layer`.
- Toast fixed bottom above app, centered, dark pill; transitions.
- Responsive tweaks.

Game stage needs full size. On mobile with notch: adbar padding-top env(safe-area-inset-top)? The app fills 100dvh; add `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)` to screen-home and game? Better handle at app level: #app { padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top); padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom); } but that would shrink. On iOS PWA perhaps. Add `padding-bottom` for home footer. Game ad banner padding. Use CSS env. Simpler add to body? We'll add `#app { padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top); padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom); }` — with background still. That reduces stage slightly and keeps gesture areas safe. But on desktop env = 0.

Need `.screen` min-height 0.

Level-specific overlay HUDs:
- `.mini-hud` absolute top 10 left 10 right 10; display flex; justify-between; pointer-events:none; z-index 5. Buttons pointer-events auto.
- `.pill` etc.
- `.upgrade-layer` absolute inset 0 z-index 8 display flex; upgrade cards.
- `.sort-toolbar` styles.
- `.level-credit` maybe.
- `.tap-hint` general.

Let's write CSS.

Now sprite loader and util modules. Then levels.

Create new sprites for survivor, slime, gem, fighter, eye-boss. Also maybe muzzle? draw. Let's write.

survivor.svg: top-down 3/4. Facing right: head at (58,38), body, gun pointing right. Need draw when rotated. Character with backpack, cap, gun. 100x100. Anchor center. We'll draw at ~40px, rotation follows aim. Make facing right (gun to x=95).

slime.svg: purple monster facing left/right? draw front-facing blob with eyes and claws; can rotate slightly to move. Use front face; small 60px, rotation not critical. Maybe bounce/flip horizontally based on vx. Draw sprite with scale(-1,1) flip.
gem.svg: cyan crystal.
fighter.svg: small white/cyan star fighter pointing up.
eye-boss.svg: giant eye with tentacles, 200x200, at top of bullet hell.

Let's create.

Detailed implementation.

```js
import { createStage, bindPointer, createKeyboard, createLoop, clamp, lerp, rand, roundRect, TAU, easeOutCubic } from '../util.js';
import { drawSprite } from '../sprites.js';
import { audio } from '../audio.js';

export const meta = {...} // main defines metadata, level only mount.

export function mount(root, api) {
  root.innerHTML = '';
  const stage = createStage(root);
  const input = createKeyboard();
  const state = {
    phase:'run', time:0, progress:0, speed:0.42, // stages per sec
    count:8, targetX:0.5, x:0.5, gates:[], pickups:[], floats:[], particles:[], shake:0,
    resultSent:false
  };
  // layout constants relative
  const gateDefs = [...]
  const gateAt = [0.62,1.5,2.4,3.3,4.2,5.1];
  gates = defs.map((def,i)=>({at: gateAt[i], ops:def.ops.sort(random side), hit:false, hitSide:null}))
```
Need sort side random for each gate? Both visible; no effect on difficulty. But visuals vary. Use shuffle.
```
function shuffleGate(g){ if(Math.random()<.5) g.ops.reverse(); }
```
Ops objects {kind:'mul'|'add', value, label}. apply = kind mul ? count*value : count+value. Values as above.

Pickups:
```
const picks = [];
for i in 0..5:
  const start = i===0?0.3:gateAt[i-1]+0.1; const end=gateAt[i]-0.1;
  const n = 2;
  for j..: at = rand(start,end); x=rand(0.18,0.82); type weighted.
```
Make 12 pickups. Maybe set positions deterministic-ish. Type weighting: coin (value 6), ally (+4), bomb (-7). The `coin` worth +6 and is gold; ally +4; bomb -7. Both positive mostly. Draw labels. To make hitting gates and pickups both possible, x random.

World coordinates: use progress in "height units". Screen y for object at world `d`: `y = playerY - (d - progress) * h`. playerY = h*0.72. Gates at d; when y == playerY → progress == d. But gates are panels with height; draw based on y center. Should trigger when their center crosses playerY? The player must be under panel; panel extends maybe 0.14h. Trigger when progress passes `d + 0.05`? Let's define gate center at screen y = playerY - (d - progress)*h. Trigger when progress >= d (center at player y). Fine. Draw panel from y-gateH/2 to y+gateH/2. Player dots at y. Good.

- Finish at d=5.85; total 13.9s. Boss appears.

- On gate crossing, determine side = x < 0.5 ? left : right; apply. Gate panels occupy entire left/right halves, so always a side.

```
const op = g.ops[side];
if op.kind==='mul' count= Math.round(count*op.value); else count += op.value;
count=Math.max(0,count);
floats.push({text:..., x, y:playerY, life:1.2, color});

audio[op.kind==='mul'?'good':'pop']...
```

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game called **AdPlay**, where each level is a real playable mini-game styled after common mobile game ads.
- User wants ads/sprites themed around mobile ad genres, explicitly including **survivor.io-style horde survival** and **bullet hell**, aimed at mobile devices.

## Requirements
- Complete, playable game; no clarifying questions; note assumptions briefly at finish.
- Mobile-first responsive experience with touch controls.
- Levels based on common mobile ad genres, including Survivor.io-like levels and bullet hell.
- Use sprites reminiscent of ads players see on phones.
- Existing build request: "This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now ... Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish."

## Decisions
- Built **7 original, ad-style mini-games** rather than copying copyrighted ad assets:
  1. Squad Rush — crowd gate runner
  2. Survivor Isle — survivor.io-style auto-shooter/horde survival with upgrade cards
  3. Bullet Heaven — bullet hell dodge/survival
  4. Knife Spin — timing/knife-throwing
  5. Snake Bites — snake.io-style growth arena
  6. Potion Sort — water-sort puzzle
  7. Dog Rescue — draw melting honey shields to block bees
- Created **original SVG sprite sheet assets** for runner variants, ogre, castle, coin, bomb, knife, apple, snake, orbs, dog, bee, survivor, slime, gem, fighter, eye boss, cloud, bush, flower.
- Implemented fake-ad chrome: sponsored-by bar, skip countdown, rotating INSTALL banner, result overlays, help sheet, sound toggle, localStorage stars/best scores, original WebAudio synth.
- All levels unlocked from start; 3-star ratings and best scores persist.
- Water-sort puzzle was verified with a BFS solver: optimal **11 moves**; stars: 3 ≤13 moves, 2 ≤18.
- Survivor has upgrade overlay choices (rapid fire, heavy rounds, multi-shot, boots, vitality, magnet, piercing).
- No build system; static `index.html` + ES modules, served by default runtime.
- Assumption to state at finish: all sprites are original recreations, not ripped ad assets.

## Work State

### Completed
- Full app shell, home screen, ad chrome, result overlays, help sheet, toast, persistence, audio.
- 7 level modules implemented.
- Original SVG sprites and sprite loader.
- Water-sort puzzle solvability verified.
- Static server running at `http://localhost:3000` via tmux session `adplay`.
- Browser smoke tests: home screen renders; Squad Rush playable/end-state reaches loss overlay; Survivor Isle runs, spawns enemies, auto-shoots, collects gems, triggers upgrade overlay.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game called **AdPlay**, where each level is a real playable mini-game styled after common mobile game ads.
- Levels should cover mobile ad genres including **survivor.io-style horde survival** and **bullet hell**, targeted at mobile devices.

## Requirements
- Complete, playable game; no clarifying questions; note assumptions briefly at finish.
- Mobile-first responsive experience with touch controls.
- Levels based on common mobile ad genres, including Survivor.io-like levels and bullet hell.
- Sprites reminiscent of ads players see on phones.
- Existing build request: "This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now ... Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish."

## Decisions
- Built **7 original, ad-style mini-games** rather than copying copyrighted ad assets:
  1. Squad Rush — crowd gate runner
  2. Survivor Isle — survivor.io-style auto-shooter/horde survival with upgrade cards
  3. Bullet Heaven — bullet hell dodge/survival
  4. Knife Spin — timing/knife-throwing
  5. Snake Bites — snake.io-style growth arena
  6. Potion Sort — water-sort puzzle
  7. Dog Rescue — draw melting honey shields to block bees
- Created **original SVG sprite sheet assets** for runner variants, ogre, castle, coin, bomb, knife, apple, snake, orbs, dog, bee, survivor, slime, gem, fighter, eye boss, cloud, bush, flower.
- Implemented fake-ad chrome: sponsored-by bar, skip countdown, rotating INSTALL banner, result overlays, help sheet, sound toggle, localStorage stars/best scores, original WebAudio synth.
- All levels unlocked from start; 3-star ratings and best scores persist.
- Water-sort puzzle verified with BFS: optimal **11 moves**; stars: 3 ≤13 moves, 2 ≤18.
- Survivor has upgrade overlay choices (rapid fire, heavy rounds, multi-shot, boots, vitality, magnet, piercing).
- No build system; static `index.html` + ES modules.
- Assumption to state at finish: all sprites are original recreations, not ripped ad assets.

## Work State

### Completed
- Full app shell, home screen, ad chrome, result overlays, help sheet, toast, persistence, audio.
- 7 level modules implemented.
- Original SVG sprites and sprite loader.
- Water-sort puzzle solvability verified.
- Static server running at `http://localhost:3000` via tmux session `adplay`.
- Fixed result-overlay redundancy: loss now shows TRY AGAIN + MENU only; win shows REPLAY (+ MENU except finale); final level shows BACK TO THE AD BREAK + REPLAY.
- Moved `.hint-chip` from `top: 50px` to `top: 76px` to avoid HUD overlap.
- Removed Survivor KILLS badge; kills now shown in bottom XP bar; player sprite enlarged 54→64.
- Patched `audio.setEnabled()` to never create/resume AudioContext at boot; autoplay warning eliminated on fresh page load.
- Removed unused `drawStars` import from `src/levels/squad.js`.
- Fixed Knife Spin keyboard input: `input.endFrame()` moved after `wasPressed` check so Space actually throws.
- Added Knife Spin input buffering (`state.queued`) for taps during flight; lowered knife collision threshold to `0.085`; verified a 3-star win (`3/3` apples).
- Verified Potion Sort win via BFS solution sequence at 11 moves, 3 stars, best-score save.
- Verified Dog Rescue loss and win; rebalanced (`LINE_LIFE 8.5`, ink 760/900, regen 60/s); win reached 2 hearts/2 stars.
- Verified Snake Bites win at size 121, 3 stars; moved its intro text to `h * 0.32` to clear the hint chip.
- Rebalanced Survivor Isle: fireInterval 0.32, damage 30, lower enemy HP/speed/spawn rate, bite damage 9/14, inv 1.0; run reached 41 kills with full HP and ~1s remaining (timer crawls under automation).
- Rebalanced Bullet Heaven slightly: inv 1.5, slower aimed shots, later spiral/rain/ring/side pattern starts.
- Mobile 390×844 home and Squad Rush layouts verified visually; home shows 7-card grid with last card scrollable.

### Active
- Final browser verification of remaining end-state flows and mobile in-game layouts.
- Desktop (1440×900) final screenshot pass not yet re-run after latest edits.
- No git commit has been made; all changes uncommitted.

### Blocked
- Browser automation runs at very low rAF frame rate (game time advances ~1/3 real time or slower), making 20–30s survival timers slow to finish.
- Survivor win overlay not yet visually captured; Bullet win not yet achieved (loss overlay verified at 8.3s).
- Squad win overlay not yet captured (loss/boss flow verified).

## Next Move
1. Verify Squad Rush win path (steer into strong multiplier gates) and capture win overlay.
2. Capture Survivor Isle win overlay if feasible; otherwise rely on code path and near-win run.
3. Retry Bullet Heaven for a win or accept loss overlay verification.
4. Re-run syntax checks for all edited modules.
5. Capture final desktop 1440×900 screenshots of home and representative levels.
6. Confirm no console errors/warnings on a fresh page load.
7. Summarize finish notes, including original-sprite assumption.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: app shell, home/game screens, ad chrome, stage/host, result layer.
- `styles.css`: visual system, responsive frame, home cards, game chrome, overlays, HUD helpers.
- `src/main.js`: level registry/metadata, routing, persistence, skip logic, results, help, audio toggle.
- `src/util.js`: canvas sizing, loop, pointer/keyboard input, math helpers.
- `src/sprites.js`: SVG preload + `drawSprite`.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized WebAudio sound kit.
- `src/levels/squad.js`: Squad Rush runner.
- `src/levels/survivor.js`: Survivor Isle auto-shooter + upgrade overlay.
- `src/levels/bullet.js`: Bullet Heaven dodge/bullet hell.
- `src/levels/knife.js`: Knife Spin.
- `src/levels/snake.js`: Snake Bites.
- `src/levels/sort.js`: Potion Sort.
- `src/levels/rescue.js`: Dog Rescue.
- `assets/sprites/`: 22 original SVG sprites.
- `screenshots/`: home, squad, survivor, potion sort, knife, snake, rescue, bullet, mobile captures.

## Important Context
- Current working directory: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`.
- Server: `PORT=3000 RUNTIME_DIR=$RUNTIME_DIR node $RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs` in tmux session `adplay`.

- Latest verified screenshots:
  - `screenshots/mobile-home.png`, `screenshots/mobile-squad.png`
  - `screenshots/sort-win.png` (3 stars, 11 moves)
  - `screenshots/knife-win5.png` (3 stars, 3/3 apples)
  - `screenshots/snake-play.png` (size 121, 3 stars)
  - `screenshots/rescue-result.png` (2 stars, 14 blocked)
  - `screenshots/survivor-final5.png` (full HP, 41 kills, 1.0s left)
  - `screenshots/bullet-run2.png` (loss overlay)
- `playwright-cli press space` does not reliably deliver keyboard events; synthetic `KeyboardEvent('keydown',{key:' ',code:'Space'})` works.
- Synthetic `PointerEvent` dispatch works for canvas input; async page evals with `setTimeout` work, but browser rAF throttling makes timed gameplay slow.
- Potion Sort solution sequence: `[[1,4],[0,1],[0,4],[2,4],[2,0],[1,2],[3,0],[3,4],[3,1],[2,3],[1,2]]`.
- Potential improvement still open: tighten home layout so more of the 7-card grid is visible without scroll.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser

Storage:
